entries.summary: Queue deletion of published external appointments
entries.description: Queues removal of ChurchTools-published appointments from the configured Evangelische Termine organizer. Local ChurchTools appointments are retained. The background job reads the external JSON event list and deletes remote dates whose external identifier starts with ChurchTools; it does not limit removal to calendars currently selected for synchronization. Requires the churchcore permission "administer settings". HTTP 204 means the deletion job was queued and started in the background, not that remote deletion has completed. If synchronization is disabled, this call returns 204 without queuing a job. It does not disable synchronization, so later synchronization can publish appointments again. There is no dry-run option or returned job identifier.

responses.description: Empty response. Deletion was queued, or synchronization is disabled and no job was queued.
The caller lacks "administer settings" in churchcore.

entries.description:
This endpoint returns birthdays within a specific time interval. The returned objects are ordered by MONTH-DAY, where the first birthday in the list is the one next from the start date.
The API also returns the `age` of the birthday. That age is calculated based on the date interval. That means, it is not the current age and also not the next birthday, but the age which the person had/will have at the end of the given date interval.
There are two ways to utilize this endpoint:
  1. With a fixed date interval (`start_date`, `end_date`). This
  interval must not be larger than one year.
  2. With a `start_date` and a `direction` field. This combination also
  accepts a `page` and `limit` parameter (both with suitable defaults)
  to paginate through the results.

entries.description: Legacy SAML URL. Resolves the single configured SAML provider; with zero or multiple SAML providers it cannot resolve a provider. Prefer the provider-specific /externallogins/{externalLoginId}/saml/login URL. Starts the browser-based SAML login for a visible SAML external-login provider. Redirects to the configured identity provider with a SAML authentication request and an opaque RelayState. An optional post-login redirect is saved in the browser session, so the callback must retain that session. Only absolute URLs on this installation’s origin and within its base path are accepted; invalid redirect values are ignored. Missing, hidden or invalid providers and other setup failures produce a localized 404 response. No login or JSON access token is returned by this endpoint itself.

entries.summary: Apply multiple raw permission changes atomically
entries.description: Applies raw permission changes atomically, including changes for different source owners. All entries are validated and authorized against the state before any writes. The authorization and locked-permission rules of the corresponding single-assignment operations apply to each entry. Any failure leaves all assignments unchanged. Duplicate owner/authId/inheritance keys are rejected.
